Safety chips are labelled by the first matching entry in a severity-ordered keyword list, over tokens common in ordinary clinical prose. The vocabulary half was approved and shipped on 2026-09-18 (cease, withhold, hold the dose, boxed warning, black box, hypersensitivity, anaphylaxis, and the immediate(?:ly)? adverb fix); that wording is a clinical judgement and remains unsigned apart from the 2026-09-25 urgent/seizure/transfer widening signed off by the owner (see the UPDATE below). CORRECTION 2026-09-19, verified against main: the second half of this decision - whether a keyword-derived finding should hold the answer's headline support position - was raised on a premise that no longer holds. It cited answerSupportPriority in src/components/clinical-dashboard/evidence-panels.tsx, which returns a safety finding ahead of the 'Review source match' caution. That function and its AnswerSupportSummaryCard have NO caller anywhere in src/: the support card was removed from the answer surface on 2026-08-31 and replaced by the Key points rail, as tests/answer-support-priority.dom.test.tsx itself asserts. The shipped surface renders RetrievalStateBanner (grounding state) and the clinical points rail (safety findings) as separate elements, both visible, banner first, so no keyword match displaces the grounding caution and there is no headline contest to decide. UPDATE 2026-09-25 (#51975R, owner decision): answerSupportPriority and AnswerSupportSummaryCard have been deleted, with their pinning tests, so no code path can promote a safety finding into a headline position any longer. What still needs a clinician is the vocabulary itself, not the ordering. UPDATE 2026-09-25 (#GHC4XZ): the owner (Josh, psychiatrist) signed off widening only the urgent tokens - red_flag now matches urgent(?:ly)? and seizures?, escalation now matches transfer(?:s|red|ring)? - as explicit suffix groups so transferrin and transference stay unlabelled. A further owner decision the same day (decision 9) excludes transfer followed by 'into' or 'across' (transfer(?:s|red|ring)?(?!\s+(?:into|across)\b)), so pharmacokinetic passages such as 'Sertraline transfers into breast milk' and 'Lithium is transferred across the placenta' get no Escalation chip; a known consequence, not separately reviewed by the owner and pinned in tests/clinical-safety.test.ts, is that a patient transfer phrased 'into' (for example 'Transfer into ICU was arranged.') also gets none. Because the first matching entry wins, this also moves some passages up a tier (to Red flag from Escalation, Dose limit, Monitoring, Exclusion and Caveat; to Escalation from Dose limit, Monitoring, Exclusion and Caveat); each measured movement is pinned in tests/clinical-safety.test.ts. review, exclude, consider and caution still miss their inflected forms (reviewed, excluded, considered, cautious); that remainder was not covered by the sign-off and stays open.

Four dictionary sources are held because the publisher field names a description rather than an agency: WA-MHAS 'Government of Western Australia', WA-AHLO 'WA Health service providers', WA-MHERL 'Mental Health Commission / WA Health' (two bodies in one field) and 4AT-OFFICIAL '4AT developers'. Establishing the real agency needs the four canonical pages read, which this environment's network policy blocks, so they stay held. Two findings do not need those pages and need a decision. (1) The register contradicts itself: source-authority-registry.ts registers 'Government of Western Australia' at line 509 (catalogue-identity only, added 2026-09-16 by commit 255b9c1fe) while the comment at lines 558-564 still states that string was deliberately not registered. One of the two is wrong and the comment misleads anyone reading it. (2) Correcting any publisher only clears the acquisition gate if the new name resolves in that register, and the register is a protected retrieval-ranking surface, so a metadata correction is also a retrieval change. Neither was edited here.

The patient-profile number fields (age, eGFR, serum creatinine, creatinine clearance, QTc) feed dose calculators, so a value displayed must never differ from the value stored. The #WFARS3 defect that broke that invariant was fixed on 2026-09-18. CORRECTION 2026-09-19, verified against main: the standing question as written - 'is it ever acceptable for the number on screen to differ from the number a dose calculation uses' - is already answered NO by the shipped field, and the answer is enforced by committed tests. A partial or out-of-range entry is refused rather than stored, the field shows the range error and sets aria-invalid, and the previously stored number is cleared rather than left behind a contradicting draft (tests/patient-profile-panel.dom.test.tsx, 'treats a partial QTc as unassessed rather than as a number under the floor'). The alternative of preserving the last good value while an entry is in progress was considered and rejected on 2026-09-19: it would reintroduce exactly the display-versus-stored disagreement this decision exists to prevent. The residual risk is narrower than first recorded and is tracked as #DTAMMK: a refused entry still survives a profile clear performed from another mounted panel.
